datasets.name: Bijie Landslide Dataset
datasets.verbatim: The Bijie Landslide Dataset, an early open-source benchmark from Wuhan University, includes 2773 images (770 landslide-positive) at 0.8 m resolution from TripleSat over 26,853 km2 of karst terrain in Guizhou, China Ji et al. (2020)

datasets.name: Landslide4Sense
datasets.verbatim: Landslide4Sense establishes a global multisource benchmark for competitions, with 3799 training, 245 validation, and 800 test patches (128 × 128 pixels) at 10 m resolution from Sentinel-2 (12 optical bands) fused with ALOS PALSAR DEM/slope data across four continents (Ghorbanzadeh et al., 2022).

datasets.name: GVLM Dataset
datasets.verbatim: The GVLM Dataset establishes the first large-scale landslide mapping benchmark, comprising 17 bitemporal image pairs (pre- and post-event) at 0.59 m resolution from Google Earth, covering 163.77 km2 across six continents including diverse sites in Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Europe, and Oceania (Zhang et al., 2023).

methods.name: GeoNeXt
methods.summary: GeoNeXt is a U-Net-style semantic segmentation architecture that combines a pre-trained ConvNeXt V2 encoder with a decoder utilizing Pyramid Squeeze Attention (PSA) and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) to capture multi-scale features for landslide recognition.
methods.verbatim: The codebase, model weights, and datasets are available at: https://github.com/ruribev/GeoNeXt/tree/main.

code_links.name: GeoNeXt codebase and model weights
code_links.summary: Custom codebase and trained model weights for the GeoNeXt method, shared alongside the datasets in the same GitHub repository.

availability.author_statement: Full availability statement, with shared links for data.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory datasets are publicly available. The custom code for the GeoNeXt method is available via a provided GitHub repository link.
